eight_gb_plateau_assessment.meaning: No exact 8 GB or 8 GiB plateau is directly established by the sampled gauges. This is not an exclusion of unobserved limits.

next_import_diagnostic.hypothesis_status: The current counters do not prove that buffered loop I/O caused the observed reclaim or timeout. This is a controlled diagnostic experiment, not an established repair.
next_import_diagnostic.selected_by_root: Controlled comparison with direct I/O enabled and read back only on the newly owned loop device, after proofstore setup and before restoration.
unchanged: historical proof-object origins and complete readback checks

observations: The same actual Lean PID/start identity is observed throughout 89 samples, with no process-read error.
The controlled process was killed by its 900-second controller timeout before any persisted phase marker; no original proof-body checkpoint was reached.
Substantial Lean-attributed storage reads and major faults continue after ordinary read-call counters stabilize; process swap is repeatedly nonzero.
The containing service cgroup records repeated anonymous/file refaults, swapin/swapout and memory-pressure stall time.
Readable non-root memory.max/high/swap.max and cpu.max are unlimited; recorded high/max/oom/oom_kill and CPU throttling counters remain zero.
The cgroup root lacks the non-root limit interfaces with explicit ENOENT; these reads are not represented as numerical zeroes.
Global SwapFree reaches 40,955,904 bytes while Lean VmSwap is 2,907,189,248 bytes; this is observed near exhaustion of free swap, not proof of a configured per-process limit.

origin.native_run_job_authentication: Separate root-owned authentication; this analysis verifies the fixed ZIP and its extracted evidence bytes

proactive_reclaim_observation.meaning: No proactive reclaim is recorded by these counters during the observed samples. This does not audit external control writes or establish that every eviction mechanism is absent.

process_identity.scope_caution: State is a sampled thread-group-leader state; it does not establish the states of all five threads.

supported_inferences: Repeated paging/reclaim is an observed performance burden in the pre-header interval. The data supports investigating import/loading/mapping behavior before changing proof bodies.
A CPU-bandwidth quota, memory.high/max event or OOM kill is not supported by the visible recorded limits/events. Other unmeasured scheduler or host constraints are not excluded.
Constant rchar/syscr with increasing storage-read and fault counters is consistent with mapped-page and swap activity; it does not identify a particular file or instruction.
timing_method: All table times are seconds since the observer began, not since Lean began. Counter deltas use stat_after from the first and last valid Lean sample. The first and final unsampled seconds are not extrapolated.
unresolved: No mmap/munmap arguments, return values or per-file mapping/fault identities were captured, so no deterministic-address collision is established.
Cgroup counters include other tasks and cannot all be attributed exclusively to Lean.
No per-thread state/wchan/stack, cpu.pressure or io.pressure was captured; total waiting time cannot be partitioned into CPU/IO/memory causes from these counters.
Logical restored file lengths, virtual address size, resident pages and storage-layer read counters are different quantities and must not be equated.
No cause is assigned to a particular module or proof declaration; successful control only establishes that the marker mechanism worked in its isolated control.
Hidden cgroup ancestors, memory.min/low protection, vm.swappiness and external supervisor policy were not directly observed; no general absence of memory constraints is claimed.
